sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Dolores Huerta, a pioneering civil rights activist and labour organiser, died in California on Wednesday aged 96. The BBC confirmed she died of cancer.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union with Cesar Chavez, securing landmark contracts, overtime pay, and protections against heat deaths for agricultural labourers. She coined the rallying cry 'Sí, se puede!', helped negotiate immigration reforms, and championed women's and voting rights across several decades.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham ruled out calling a general election in the next 12 months. Opposition leaders Kemi Badenoch and Nigel Farage had claimed Burnham would hold an early vote. Burnham also told cabinet ministers not to express personal opinions on future EU relations.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Opposition figures argued Burnham lacks a mandate after becoming prime minister following Sir Keir Starmer's resignation. Burnham countered that the Conservative Brexit deal caused low growth, but insisted government policy on EU relations must remain disciplined during this parliamentary term.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Burnham will attend a European summit next month to discuss initial Brexit changes within manifesto limits. Any major alterations to the UK's relationship with the EU will form part of a 10-year plan for the public to decide after the next election.

gist: Built-up land in high-risk Himalayan zones grew by about 45% between 2016 and 2023.
At least 300,000 people now live in the path of potential Himalayan disasters.
Rapid warming speeds up glacier melting, destabilising slopes and expanding glacial lakes.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A new study reveals that built-up land in high-risk zones across northern Nepal, Tibet, and India's Uttarakhand increased by roughly 45% between 2016 and 2023. Areas threatened by glacial lake flooding saw development rise by almost 78%. Tourism facilities, real estate, and infrastructure expanded rapidly along river banks and trekking regions.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Warming in the Himalayas occurs at twice the global rate, accelerating glacier melt and destabilising mountain slopes. This increases the risk of catastrophic floods and landslides, threatening at least 300,000 people. Campaigners note that building regulations are poorly enforced and development has occurred without proper planning.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Authorities in Nepal plan to ban settlements within 15m of riverbanks along specific corridors, and Uttarakhand approved new floodplain zoning rules. However, experts warn that mitigating threats completely will remain a major challenge.

fivew: Researchers from the UK, Nepal, and India.
A study found significant development growth in high-risk Himalayan disaster zones.
Northern Nepal, south-eastern Tibet, and Uttarakhand in India.
Tourism, housing, and infrastructure expansion have outpaced safety planning amid regional warming.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: China expelled 33 members from the Communist Party at the fifth plenum, a closed-door gathering in Beijing. Attendance fell to 279 members, marking the highest number of empty seats in modern Chinese history. High-ranking figures removed include former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui and top military figures Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The purges have gutted the Central Military Commission down to just two members, raising questions about military leadership and combat readiness. Observers note the campaign consolidates Xi Jinping's authority and targets disloyalty as he prepares for potential leadership changes.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The plenum laid groundwork for the next Party Congress in 2027, where analysts expect Xi to secure a fourth term. Xi will likely dominate personnel selections to fill the gaps left by the recent expulsions.

gist: A second fatal high-speed train collision in Spain has killed at least 69 people.
Leaked audio suggests computer and human errors caused the crash near Urda.
The disaster has intensified political pressure on Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez before elections.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A Renfe train rammed a stationary Iryo train from behind on the Madrid-Seville line near Urda, killing at least 69 people. The disaster follows a rail crash in January that killed 46 people. Leaked control-room audio suggested a computer failure and human error caused the collision.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The tragedy occurred a month before a snap general election, disrupting political campaigning across Spain. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his transport minister, Óscar Puente, face heavy criticism over rail safety. Conservative and far-right opposition parties have used the disaster to attack the government's management of public infrastructure.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Spain's main train drivers' union, Semaf, called a strike to demand that safety be prioritised over travel urgency. Opposition politicians are demanding accountability, while Vox has urged the Supreme Court to investigate Puente. Rail safety is expected to dominate the upcoming general election campaign.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 employees across multiple regions to lower operating costs and support AI infrastructure investments. Meanwhile, Denmark ended its trial moving away from Microsoft Office after encountering formatting and tracking issues. In gaming and leadership, Xbox executives departed, and Microsoft merged its Forza developers.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The workforce reductions signal how artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing Microsoft's staffing needs and operating costs. Additionally, Denmark's return to Microsoft software highlights the ongoing reliance on established US tech vendors despite efforts to diversify.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Eligible employees have until December to decide on the buyout offers, which will inform Microsoft's upcoming headcount numbers and potential further cuts.

He worked as a producer, arranger, and composer throughout his career.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Dónal Lunny, a prominent multi-instrumentalist, arranger and producer in Irish traditional music, died of cancer at the age of 79. He was known for playing the guitar, keyboards and bodhrán, and for popularising the Irish bouzouki. Throughout his career, he played in major folk bands including Planxty, the Bothy Band and Moving Hearts, and collaborated with numerous artists.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Lunny played a vital role in shaping traditional Irish music by developing new harmonic and rhythmic structures and forming highly influential groups. His work spanned successful band recordings, production, film and television composition, and cross-genre collaborations with prominent international artists.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Experts writing in the Lancet published a report calling for the government to treat the manosphere and online misogyny as public health issues. They describe the manosphere as a lucrative commercial ecosystem that profits from extreme misogyny and male grievance.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Young men facing loneliness, economic worries, and educational disengagement are vulnerable to online communities that blame feminism. Commercial models reward outrage, mirroring tactics used by the tobacco industry.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The chief executive of California’s high-speed rail authority, Ian Choudri, resigned abruptly on Wednesday. This followed a September investigative report from the state’s office of the inspector general that found the agency paid $543,000 in disallowed travel reimbursements for consultants, including money spent on gyms, an escape room and a nightclub. Choudri cited personal priorities in his resignation email, and Joe Stephenshaw was appointed as interim CEO.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The rail project has become a major financial and political headache for California. Eighteen years after voters approved it, no tracks have been laid, costs have soared above $100bn, and $4bn in federal funding was withdrawn last year. Potential gubernatorial candidates have also signaled that major staff changes are necessary to restore public confidence.

sections.text: Detectives in Scotland joined international efforts to target online gangs known as The Com. These groups groom and coerce vulnerable children, mostly young girls, into acts of self-harm and abuse on gaming platforms and social media. Police have identified victims and perpetrators in Scotland, with one arrest made so far.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts describe the networks as representing the gravest risk to children online. Abusers exploit young people for kudos or clout, escalating harm through manipulation and blackmail. While the scale is considered low-volume, the harm caused is extreme.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Police forces across the UK continue to investigate and map the threat. The Molly Rose Foundation urged action from regulators and leaders, while Ofcom stated it is working closely with law enforcement and will act against services failing to comply with duties.

sections.text: An evacuation corridor opened from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky following a ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Evacuees travel into Russian-occupied territory, on to Anapa, fly to Gomel, and drive into Ukraine. Several hundred residents remain.

gist: US death row inmate Christa Pike released her first statement following a botched execution.
Pike reported experiencing continuous physical pain, mental suffering and medical complications after surviving.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused executions while an independent review investigates the failed procedure.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Christa Pike survived a failed lethal injection on 30 September in Tennessee. Execution staff spent nearly an hour attempting to establish an intravenous line to administer pentobarbital. Pike spent ten days in intensive care suffering from pneumonia, severe swelling and swallowing difficulties before returning to a rehabilitation centre infirmary. She subsequently released a statement describing constant physical pain, mental anguish and isolation, whilst criticising official incompetence.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Pike is believed to be the only person to survive a lethal injection execution attempt. The botched procedure sparked widespread international shock. Slemmer's mother described the execution as a mess and demanded an apology, whilst the Tennessee Department of Correction defended its execution method.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused all executions for the rest of the year and ordered an independent review into the botched event. Lee indicated that Pike's death sentence will remain unchanged unless court rulings determine otherwise.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US stocks slid as concerns grew over artificial intelligence costs. Intel shares fell up to 30 percent after warning of a weaker computer market while increasing AI spending. Reddit and Roblox shares also declined following weaker-than-expected user figures.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The losses follow Alphabet's market value dropping by more than $500bn after AI summaries affected search advertising revenue. Analysts question the payout from huge AI investments as major tech firms show growing pains from aggressive expansion.

gist: Russell Brand gave evidence at his trial, denying all charges.
He stated that allegations and documentaries caused severe personal and professional impact.
The trial at Southwark Crown Court continues.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Russell Brand took the witness stand at Southwark Crown Court. He denied multiple charges of sexual offences involving six complainants across a decade. During questioning by his defence barrister, Brand stated that consent is essential and denied committing any of the alleged acts.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The entertainer testified that publicity surrounding the claims affected his life and relationships deeply. He described losing support from peers and being barred from a hospital where his child underwent surgery.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The legal proceedings at Southwark Crown Court are ongoing as the trial continues.

fivew: Russell Brand gave evidence denying several sexual offence charges at his trial.

timeline.text: 'The most important person managers must manage is themselves'

gist: Management workload is extremely time-consuming and stressful.
Early in his career, the author neglected his health.
Prioritising fitness, family, and avoiding media helped manage stress.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The author began his first management job at Bournemouth in 1992, taking on vast responsibilities under immense pressure. His health suffered until a triathlete gave him advice in 1994, leading him to prioritise fitness.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Football management involves relentless demands and severe stress that can endanger a manager's health and wellbeing if they do not look after themselves.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Managers now benefit from much more support, including health testing from the League Managers' Association and medical staff looking after coaching personnel.

fivew: A football manager shares how he learned to manage his own health and stress.
During his career starting in 1992 at Bournemouth.
To advise young managers on coping with the relentless stress of the job.

articles.standfirst: Ben Duckett hits 167 and Liam Dawson takes four wickets as England end the tri-series with victory over Sri Lanka.

timeline.text: Duckett and Dawson deliver in England's consolation win

gist: Ben Duckett scored a massive century for England in Lahore.
Liam Dawson took four crucial wickets to secure a consolation victory.
Sri Lanka fell short despite Pavan Rathnayake's brilliant century.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England posted a huge total of 386-5 driven by Duckett and Tom Banton. Sri Lanka chased bravely through Rathnayake and Kusal Mendis, but collapsed near the end to lose by 55 runs.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The high scoring match gave England a morale boosting win in the tri series while providing selectors with difficult choices regarding squad depth and opening batters.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Sri Lanka will face Pakistan in the tri series final. Meanwhile England are scheduled to travel onwards for fixtures in Australia.

fivew: England players Ben Duckett and Liam Dawson.
England defeated Sri Lanka by 55 runs in a high scoring one day international.
During the tri series final match phase.
To conclude their tri series campaign with a win.

quotes.text: You want options, and guys to push their case when they get their opportunities

gist: Lewis Hamilton believes he is unlike any driver Formula 1 has seen before.
The seven-time world champion intends to keep racing into his mid-forties.
Hamilton aims to fulfil a dream of racing at a new Grand Prix in Africa.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Lewis Hamilton stated at a news conference ahead of the Mexico Grand Prix that he is unlike any previous Formula 1 driver and plans to continue racing into his mid-forties.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Hamilton wants to fulfil a long-held ambition to race in Africa. Formula 1 has recently signed a ten-year agreement with Rwanda to host a race beginning in the early 2030s.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Hamilton remains fully committed to the sport for the foreseeable future, despite acknowledging potential age-related challenges ahead.

gist: Fleetwood Town will play either Everton or Newcastle United in the quarter-finals.
The League Two team advanced by defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout.
The quarter-final matches are scheduled for the week starting 14 December.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Fleetwood Town advanced to the quarter-finals after overcoming Arsenal on penalties. They will now face the winners of the match between Everton and Newcastle United. Meanwhile, holders Manchester City were drawn against Bradford City, Liverpool will play Bournemouth, and Crystal Palace face Sunderland.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Fleetwood Town are the lowest-ranked club remaining in the tournament and have achieved a historic milestone by reaching the final eight.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Fleetwood await the conclusion of the fourth-round fixture between Everton and Newcastle to discover their specific opponent. The quarter-final ties are scheduled to occur during the week beginning 14 December.

gist: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or at the London Palladium.
His career included challenging loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City, and Leicester City.
He achieved success at Tottenham Hotspur, Bayern Munich, and for England.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or at the London Palladium, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. His career included loan spells at lower division clubs before breaking through at Tottenham Hotspur and later moving to Bayern Munich.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: He became the first English player to win the trophy since 2001 and the fifth overall, proving his doubters wrong through hard work and dedication.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: After celebrations, Kane returns to business with Bayern Munich playing Magdeburg and Borussia Dortmund, while targeting potential success with England at Euro 2028.

fivew: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or.
His exemplary career and goalscoring success for club and country.

quotes.text: Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise.
